A 6-year-old boy is brought to the emergency department by his father for elbow pain.
On exam, the boy is holding his right wrist with his left hand and cries upon palpation of a region that is 2 cm proximal to his elbow.
The radial head is palpated just distal to the lateral epicondyle.
He is unable to make a pincer with his right thumb and index finger.
The radial pulse is diminished on the right.
He was riding his bicycle when he fell onto his outstretched right hand.
He immediately clutched his right elbow in pain and began crying.
